{{Quote|''[''S'']''uch very different ways of writing as the Aurebesh, the ancient Durese syllabary, the Pre-Corellian alphabet, and the abjad of the Azure Imperium all use symbols from Rakatan sources, rarely in the same ways.|Doctor Milanda Vorgan, "The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic"|<ref name="Written" />}}
The '''abjad of the Azure Imperium''' was a [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] used in the [[Azure Imperium]],<ref name="Written" /> an interstellar civilization centered on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Axum]] and established before the [[Galactic Constitution Conference|formation]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="CCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> The abjad used characters that were derived from the logographic [[Rakatan writing system|writing system]] of<ref name="Written" /> [[Rakata (language)|Rakata]], the [[Language/Legends|language]] spoken by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]],<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> which had at one point [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] the inhabitants of the Azure Imperium. The latter faction's script shared this re-use of Rakata symbols with various other, very different writing systems&mdash;such as the [[ancient Durese syllabary]] and the [[Pre-Corellian alphabet|Pre-Corellian]] and [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] alphabets&mdash;which frequently adopted the glyphs with no apparent connection to the original logographic nature of the Rakatan script. The abjad of the Azure Imperium's Rakatan origins were eventually noted by the [[Xenolinguist/Legends|xenolinguist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Milanda Vorgan]] in<ref name="Written" /> her<ref name="TT">{{WEGCite|story=Erasing All Traces|book=The Last Command Sourcebook|reprint=1}}</ref> [[38 ABY]] publication "[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]."<ref name="Written" />

==Behind the scenes==
The abjad of the Azure Imperium was introduced in the article "[[The Written Word]]," which was authored by [[John Hazlett]] and published on [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] on [[March 5]], [[2010]].<ref name="Written" /> In the real world, the term "[[Wikipedia:Abjad|abjad]]" denotes a writing system in which characters represent primarily [[Wikipedia:Consonant|consonants]] and few or no [[Wikipedia:Vowel|vowels]].<ref name="Abjad">{{WebCite|url=https://www.dictionary.com/browse/abjad|text=ABJAD Definition & Usage Examples|work=[[Wikipedia:Dictionary.com|Dictionary.com]]|quote=a system of writing, as in Hebrew and Arabic scripts, in which each symbol represents a consonantal sound, with few or no vowels being represented in the basic characters.|archivedate=20240103062052}}</ref>
